claims.text: The target material is a Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy with density below 6 g/cm3.
The initial as-cast microstructure contains a supersaturated, metastable solid-solution matrix.
Fine, under-equilibrated intermetallic particles are dispersed in the initial matrix.
Thermal exposure below melting permits diffusion-driven evolution of the metastable microstructure.
Metastable intermetallic precursors form and grow into stabilized intermetallic compounds during thermal exposure.
Mg, Al, and other alloying elements have differential diffusivities that cause phase separation in the metastable matrix.
Transformation of non-equilibrium intermetallic particles changes local elemental distributions and electrochemical potentials.
The evolved local chemistry reduces the number or severity of anodic micro-galvanic corrosion sites.
Phase evolution promotes more uniform, coherent, continuous, and adherent protective oxide scales.
The protective high-temperature oxide scale can include MgO and Al2O3.
Annealed or thermally exposed samples will contain more clearly defined stable intermetallic phases than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed or thermally exposed samples will develop a more uniform and adherent protective oxide layer than the as-cast baseline.
The evolved microstructure will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast baseline.
The evolved microstructure may produce lower or more stable corrosion current densities than the as-cast baseline.
The corrosion response depends on interphase spacing and oxide quality.
The proposed behavior is limited to non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight alloys whose metastable phases can evolve during post-processing thermal exposure.
Alloys that strongly favor equilibrium segregation from the start may behave differently.
Mg-Zn, Mg-Ti, and Zn-Ti systems provide prior observations that oxide-rich or Ti-rich surface phases can improve passivation and reduce corrosion current.

Al-Cu-Si-Zn-Mg and Al-Mn-Zn-Mg-Si lightweight complex concentrated alloys have been reported to retain solid-solution-based structures in as-cast and heat-treated conditions while containing several intermetallic phases.

contradictions.description: The intervention allows service in an oxidizing or corrosive environment to drive diffusion, but the corrosion example is NaCl solution without a specified elevated temperature. Such a test can measure corrosion without necessarily providing the thermal activation required for the proposed phase evolution.
